title: Lost Speed? Momentum Conserved Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A carrom striker slows down as the coin shoots away. A gun kicks back as it fires. And when Aarav's friend on a skateboard grabs his coasting bike, they both roll slower, with nobody braking. Where did the speed go? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn the law of conservation of linear momentum and use it to predict the new speed.

On a live motion notebook two carts crash and stick, then bounce off a spring bumper, then push apart from rest, while the readout and a momentum vs time graph show p of each cart changing and the total staying perfectly flat. A slow-mo replay freezes the crash to show the equal and opposite forces, and we prove the law from Newton's third law step by step. Then the gun's recoil link by link, internal vs external forces side by side, two pause-and-think questions, a worked example, the exam trap (momentum adds as a vector), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Where did the speed go?
0:28 Momentum, a system, and the law
0:53 Motion notebook: two carts, one total
1:21 Slow-mo replay: equal and opposite forces
2:05 The proof from the third law, in five steps
2:51 Why a gun kicks back, link by link
3:17 Side by side + pause and think
3:49 Worked example: Aarav and his friend
4:25 Exam trap: add momentum as vectors
4:46 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:28 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Free-Body Diagrams. A block on a rough floor has four forces on it. Can you find them all?
